cita: Chukkapalli, D., Avula, T., Aggarwal, A., Singh, H., & Tallanki, A. (2026). CommitDistill: A Lightweight Knowledge-Centric Memory Layer for Software Repositories.
problema: Developers and AI coding assistants rarely reuse the tacit engineering knowledge (constraints, fixes, recurring failure modes) buried in git commit history; existing repo-aware assistants only retrieve raw text spans, not typed distilled units.
mecanismo: Two-phase system: a deterministic regex-based extractor (Algorithm 1) mines commit messages into three typed knowledge units (Facts/constraints, Skills/actionable fixes, Patterns/failure modes) with commit-level provenance, deduplicated via content hash, stored as plain JSON; a length-normalized TF-IDF retriever (Algorithm 2) with per-type boosting (Patterns x1.2, Skills x1.1, Facts x1.0) and a calibrated silence threshold (theta=2.5) abstains rather than guessing on out-of-distribution queries.
evaluacion: Illustrative case study (not hypothesis-testing) on 5 public repos (25,000 commits, Python/JS/C/Java): RQ1 yield by type, RQ2 dual-annotated useful-precision (n=40 units, Cohen's kappa), RQ3 retrieval hit-rate vs git log --grep and BM25 (36 queries + budget-constrained 12-query benchmark), RQ4 out-of-design regression-finding stress test, RQ5 paired 4-arm LLM-as-judge downstream evaluation (n=200 time-travel bug-fixes, two judge models).
numeros_clave: 1,167 units extracted from 25,000 commits (46.7 units/kc avg, redis outlier 185.6/kc); useful-precision 0.525 at Cohen's kappa=0.633 (n=40 dual-annotated); budget-constrained (256-char/query) hit-rate: CommitDistill 0.750 vs BM25 0.333 vs git log --grep 0.083 (12-query benchmark); 36-query baseline hit-rate improved 14/36 to 31/36 via identifier-aware tokenisation; extraction of 10,000 commits under 4s; RQ5 (n=200): no statistically detectable mean lift over no-retrieval control for any retriever, CD-Hybrid indistinguishable from BM25.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Stores knowledge units as plain JSON committed to the repo, git-diffable and PR-reviewable (Table I 'Inspect.' column, section III-D) — confirms MF's docs-as-truth typed-narrative stance.

The calibrated silence threshold theta=2.5 (section III-C, VI-E) that abstains rather than guessing on out-of-corpus queries is a concrete abstention mechanism MF could adopt for negative-knowledge signaling.

The paired 4-arm LLM-judge study (n=200, section VI-G2) found no statistically detectable downstream lift from retrieval-augmented context over a no-retrieval control — challenges the assumption that typed-memory retrieval automatically helps agent task performance.

Extraction over 10k commits in under 4s and sub-50ms per-query retrieval (section III-C) show deterministic non-embedding typed memory can be near-zero marginal cost, aligning with MF's cost-economy priority.

notes: Ancla: Table II (section VI-A) yield numbers; RQ5 four-arm result in section VI-G2 (n=200, two judges). Clearly on-topic; no RECONSIDERAR needed.

cita: Guo et al. (2026). Scaling Expert Feedback with Reflective Edit Propagation in Compositional Knowledge Bases.
problema: Domain-specific knowledge bases with compositional identifiers (symbols reused across many entries) accumulate technical inaccuracies from LLM-drafted content, and a single expert's local correct-and-save edit does not propagate to the many other entries sharing the corrected symbol, making expert review at scale impractical.
mecanismo: RAID is a three-stage reflective agent: (1) Intent Inference compares the expert's edited text to the original to classify the correction (semantic-confusion, granularity, or surface-only requiring no propagation); (2) Reflection-based Planning emits a chain-of-tools plan (Update Description, NL Search, Generate New Description) that searches for identifiers sharing the corrected symbol; (3) User Controlled Execution presents each plan step as a reviewable card (search scope, generated revisions) that the human expert must explicitly approve before the next step activates, so the agent never applies a propagated correction unsupervised.
evaluacion: Quantitative benchmark on public RxTerms drug terminology (240 synthetic perturbed descriptions across 3 error types, gemini-2.5-flash injecting errors into gpt-5-mini reference text, affecting 2,744 identifiers), measuring intent-classification accuracy, propagation precision/recall/F1, revision accuracy, and cosine similarity to ground truth; plus a qualitative user study with 4 SMEs on a proprietary semiconductor-test KB using UMUX-Lite usability scoring and semi-structured interviews.
numeros_clave: Overall (Table 2): intent accuracy 99.6% (1/240 misclassified), propagation precision 98.6% / recall 100.0% / F1 99.3%, revision accuracy 76.3% (93.9% semantic-confusion, 87.9% granularity, only 49.7% surface-rephrase by design), cosine similarity 89.1%; 159/160 propagating edits executed cleanly across 2,744 identifiers, 6 edits caused 139 false-positive retrievals (all substring-collision, e.g. tretinoin/isotretinoin) cascading into 115 false revisions; user study: mean UMUX-Lite 3.75, intent-inference quality 4/5 (n=4 SMEs).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: RAID treats each symbol/identifier description as a typed, human-validated narrative entry that the human expert approves before write (section 2.1 User Controlled Execution) — confirms MF's docs-as-verifiable-truth stance.

Reflective edit propagation (section 2.1) is a concrete mechanism for promoting one expert correction into a systematic update across all structurally related entries — a pattern MF could adopt for propagating a single gotcha-fix to all affected recipes.

Every propagated change requires explicit human sign-off before being applied (section 2.1, 'the system does not apply changes immediately') — a concrete provenance/anti-drift safeguard supporting MF's FIDELIDAD anchor.

notes: Ancla: Table 2 (section 3.1) + error analysis (substring-collision false positives) + user study section 3.2 (n=4 SMEs, UMUX-Lite). Clearly on-topic human-in-the-loop KB consolidation paper.

cita: Li, X., Zang, Y., Cao, Y., & Sun, A. (2026). Skill-as-Pseudocode: Refactoring Skill Libraries to Pseudocode for LLM Agents.
problema: Markdown skill libraries for LLM agents ship as free-form prose, forcing the agent to re-derive both the input schema and the concrete invocation syntax on every retrieval, producing a 'confused -> re-retrieve -> still confused' loop that drives both task failures and per-game LLM-call cost.
mecanismo: Skill-as-Pseudocode (SaP) clusters similar procedural passages across markdown skills, drafts a typed contract (trigger/input schema/output schema/pre-post-conditions) via one LLM call per cluster, then runs a four-check DETERMINISTIC verifier (Coverage, Binding, Replacement, Risk) before promoting a contract and rewriting matching units into invoke() placeholders; two LLM-aware post-verifier passes (Binding Extraction, Rewrite Cleanup) ground call-sites and remove residual prose conflicts, each guarded by a deterministic post-check. At retrieval time the agent receives a substituted bundle: concrete action templates (how), the rewritten parent skeleton, and the inlined typed contract (what) for every invoke() placeholder, instead of bare prose.
evaluacion: ALFWorld unseen split (134 games, gpt-4o-mini, pooled across 3 seeds, n=402 paired games) comparing SaP vs the Graph-of-Skills (GoS) retrieval baseline and an ALL_FULL full-library pilot, measured via reward (paired McNemar) and token/LLM-call cost; a 10-task SkillsBench subset (gpt-5-codex, Docker coding tasks) as a second-domain generality check; and a pipeline-component ablation (deterministic-only vs +Rewrite-Cleanup vs +Binding-Extraction) on a 20-game pilot.
numeros_clave: ALFWorld (n=402 pooled): SaP wins 82/402 vs GoS 47/402 (+74% relative, pooled McNemar p=8.2e-5); concurrent savings -22.8+/-6.4% input tokens, -17.3+/-5.1% output tokens, -14.5+/-4.1% LLM calls/game. Pipeline yield on skills_500: 5,709 procedural units -> 149 clusters -> 80 auto-promoted contracts (0% FP on adversarial controls); Binding Extraction confirms 1,475/2,105 call-sites (70%, drops 30% as spurious); Rewrite Cleanup succeeds on 320/322 (99.4%) touched parents. SkillsBench 10-task subset: SaP 3/10 wins vs GoS 2/10 at -43% input tokens. Ablation: deterministic-only -> +RC -> +BE each add roughly +5pp reward (20-game pilot).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: SaP's conversion of free-prose skill docs into a typed contract + concrete-template bundle delivered at retrieval time (Figure 2, section 3.5) offers MF a concrete mechanism for turning prose narrative into typed structure without losing the executable 'how'.
The measured SIMULTANEOUS reward gain and token/LLM-call reduction on ALFWorld (Table 1, not a tradeoff) confirms typed retrieval representations are a real lever for context economy.

The retrieval-pool ablation (section 'Cross-parent factoring', children surfaced as standalone results drop reward 27%) is a measured-retrieval design lesson supporting MF's need to test retrieval configurations empirically, not assume them.

The four-check deterministic verifier plus deterministic post-checks on the two LLM-aware passes (section 3.3-3.4) ensure a promoted contract never silently drifts from the source prose, aligning with MF's anti-drift FIDELIDAD anchor.

notes: Ancla: Table 1 (main ALFWorld result, n=402) + Table 3 ablation (20-game pilot) + section 5.5-adjacent retrieval-pool ablation (children as standalone drop reward 27%). Clearly on-topic; no RECONSIDERAR needed.

cita: Li, R., Zhang, Y., Zhou, X., Cai, Y., Liang, P., Sun, W., Xuan, J., Jin, Z., & Liu, Y. (2026). Bridging Requirements and Architecture: Multi-Agent Orchestration with External Knowledge and Hierarchical Memory.
problema: Software architecture design is knowledge-intensive and traditionally architect-driven; single-agent LLM approaches yield inconsistent cross-view architectures and incomplete requirements coverage, while existing multi-agent frameworks (e.g. MetaGPT) are code-centric and lack domain-grounded reasoning, systematic quality evaluation, and reuse of prior design experience across projects.
mecanismo: MAAD orchestrates four role-specialized agents (Analyst, Modeler, Designer, Evaluator) in an iterative, feedback-driven pipeline from a Software Requirements Specification to multi-view '4+1' architecture documentation, injecting RAG-retrieved architectural standards/patterns. It is backed by a three-tier hierarchical memory: per-agent working memory (current design context/artifacts), per-agent episodic memory (design-experience records from past interactions), and a framework-level shared semantic memory (generalized architectural knowledge distilled across projects/literature) queryable by all agents, enabling knowledge accumulation/reuse and reduced recurrence of past design issues across iterative refinement.
evaluacion: Comparative evaluation against MetaGPT across 10 real-world SRS case studies (public + industrial cyber-physical-systems requirements) using structural architecture metrics (Coupling Degree, Cohesion, Interface Complexity, Structural Complexity, etc.), an ablation of RAG-based knowledge infusion (Table 4, with/without RAG across the 10 projects), a foundational-LLM comparison (GPT-5.2, Qwen3.5, DeepSeek-R1, Llama3.3; Table 5), and semi-structured interviews with 6 industry software architects for qualitative practitioner validation.
numeros_clave: Table 4 (RAG ablation, 10 projects): Component Coupling Density decreases in 6/10 projects with RAG; Cohesion decreases in 8/10 projects (attributed to finer role separation, not necessarily worse design); Coupling Degree mixed (down in 4, up in 5, unchanged in 1). Table 5 (LLM comparison): GPT-5.2/Qwen3.5 reach low Structural Complexity (SC=0.02/0.03) and high Interface Complexity (IC=2.34/2.08) vs Llama3.3's SC=0.17 (few classes but densely interconnected). Qualitative validation via 6 practitioner-architect interviews.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: MAAD's Evaluator agent produces structured, versioned architecture artifacts (ATAM report, mismatch analysis) at every stage, gated before acceptance (section 3.1) — confirms MF's docs-as-verifiable-truth stance for typed narrative artifacts.

The 3-tier working/episodic/semantic memory (section 3.3) is a concrete pattern MF could adopt: per-agent episodic experience is distilled into a framework-level shared semantic store reused across projects, analogous to MF's gotcha-to-recipe promotion.
A single shared semantic-memory store queried by all four agents (section 3.1), rather than per-agent knowledge silos, is a candidate pattern for MF's single-source-per-fact seam.

The RAG ablation (Table 4) shows knowledge infusion has a context-dependent, non-uniform effect on measured architecture-quality metrics (mixed Coupling Degree sign, Cohesion drops in 8/10) — a measured-retrieval result without a clean directional verdict.

notes: Ancla: Table 4 (RAG ablation across 10 SRS projects, section 6) + Table 5 (LLM comparison) + section 4.2.5 six-architect interview protocol. Clearly on-topic multi-agent architecture-design memory paper.

cita: Chen et al. (2026). Exploring Cross-Scenario Generality of Agentic Memory Systems: Diagnostics and a Strong Baseline.
problema: Most agentic-memory systems are tuned to a single scenario (multi-session chat OR one agentic-trajectory format) and there is little evidence they generalize across the heterogeneous trajectory types agents actually encounter in deployment (chat, agentic-trajectory QA, memory stress tests, long-horizon tasks); winning on one benchmark says nothing about the others.
mecanismo: Diagnoses two build-time failure modes in index-based memory (graph/note/multi-store): a representation-level failure where step- and action-level evidence never enters the build-time schema and is unrecoverable even by an oracle (e.g. HippoRAG's entity-relation KG drops step indices), and a retrieval-level failure where the evidence IS in storage but a passive similarity-routed retriever never surfaces it (PlugMem/AMA-Agent retain 83-98% of the answer in storage yet fail on live retrieval). Proposes AutoMEM, an agentic memory harness that defers structure commitment from build-time to query-time: at each step the agent picks among rg (regex), read (fetch by id), dump (send corpus to answer LLM), or index_query (typed query against a pre-built index), iterating under an LLM-judge sufficiency check, so retrieval strategy is chosen per-question rather than frozen at index-build time.
evaluacion: Cross-scenario evaluation of 8 memory systems plus an agent-harness baseline (DCI-Lite) across 5 task families/benchmarks (LoCoMo personal-chat, HotpotQA large-corpus retrieval, AMABench trajectory-recall, MemoryAgentBench stress tests, ALFWorld/MemoryArena real agentic tasks), tracking accuracy (LLM-judge scores / task success), token cost, and latency; includes an oracle 'storage answerability' probe (Table 4) isolating storage vs retrieval failure, controlled ablations (Table 5, Table 6 structural-rate correlation), and a GRPO-post-training vs golden-procedural-memory comparison on ALFWorld (Table 7).
numeros_clave: Generality rank (Table 3): DCI-Lite agent harness best overall generality, no index-based method dominates. Oracle storage-answerability (Table 4): PlugMem/AMA-Agent retain 83-98% of answer info in storage yet score far lower on live retrieval (pure retrieval-layer failure); HippoRAG only ~10-19% recoverable on some question types (representation-layer ceiling). AutoMEM beats DCI-Lite on LoCoMo by +22.3pp (67.3 vs 45.0), beats long-context by +5.8pp (61.5 vs 67.3), edges best baseline Mem-T by +0.8pp (66.5); reported as 49.6% improvement over the original agent harness on LoCoMo and 24.4% improvement in overall ranking. ALFWorld (Table 7, Qwen2.5-7B actor): vanilla long-context 46.7% SR, best memory method only 43.3%, golden hand-crafted procedural memory 71.7%, GRPO post-training 86.7%. Amortization crossover (Fig.3): LightMem beats DCI-Lite at N~2 shared questions, HippoRAG at N~32.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: On agentic-trajectory QA, pre-committed typed schemas (graphs/notes) lose step/action-level evidence at build time and are beaten by a flat-text grep/read harness (Table 3, Figure 2) — challenges an unconditional 'typed structure beats flat retrieval' reading, though Table 6 shows typed indexing wins when structural rate is high, so the correct MF reading is conditional, not blanket.

The oracle storage-answerability probe (Table 4) explicitly separates storage failure from retrieval failure and shows retrieval-layer failure dominates for episodic-rich stores — strong confirmation that MF's retrieval layer must be MEASURED, not assumed correct once storage exists.

Token cost and latency are tracked alongside accuracy for every method (Figure 1) and an explicit amortization break-even (N~2 vs N~32, Figure 3) is derived, confirming MF's stance that index/build cost only pays off past a workload-dependent threshold.

Section 4.5 shows a hand-distilled 'golden' procedural memory massively outperforms self-summarized episodic reflections (71.7% vs 43.3% ALFWorld SR) because a weaker actor cannot reliably distill reusable recipes from its own trajectories — implies MF's consolidation step may need a higher-capability distiller, not pure self-summarization.

notes: Ancla: Table 3 (main cross-benchmark results) + Table 4 (oracle storage-answerability probe, key evidence) + Table 7 (ALFWorld golden-memory vs GRPO, section 4.5). Directly on-topic cross-scenario memory generality study.

cita: Ji et al. (2026). Infini Memory: Maintainable Topic Documents for Long-Term LLM Agent Memory.
problema: Existing persistent LLM-agent memory systems (isolated records, summaries, vector/graph indices) exhibit four recurring failure modes: memory fragmentation (related evidence scattered across many small records), memory conflict (append-only storage leaves both old and new contradictory facts retrievable), long-history compression loss (summarization erases temporal/source cues), and retrieval insufficiency (single-shot top-k retrieval returns isolated fragments rather than enough context for temporally grounded multi-hop reasoning).
mecanismo: Infini Memory represents persistent memory as a library of topic-structured plain-text documents (metadata header + hierarchical body of timestamped/sourced entries) instead of atomic records or a graph/vector index. New extracted memories are appended to a short-term CURRENT buffer rather than written directly into the topic library; when the buffer crosses a token/time threshold it is rewritten, deduplicated, and routed by a planner into existing or new topic documents (splitting oversized docs, merging small ones), decoupling consolidation from write frequency. At query time an agentic reader iteratively calls memory tools (grep/search/list_docs/read_lines) over the topic library plus the CURRENT buffer, expanding matched entries into their local coherent block using seq/time/source metadata instead of returning bare fragments, with a lexical BM25 fallback as a recall guard.
evaluacion: Evaluated on MemoryAgentBench across its four capabilities (Accurate Retrieval, Test-Time Learning, Long-Range Understanding, Selective Forgetting) against 7 baselines (RAPTOR, MemoRAG, HippoRAG-v2, Mem0, MemGPT, LightMem, REMem) using gpt-5-mini as backbone and gpt-5 as LLM-judge; compares a hybrid (LLM-summary + BM25) reader vs an agentic multi-tool-call reader, plus a retrieval-strategy ablation isolating single-shot-summary vs +BM25 vs +agentic gains.
numeros_clave: Infini Memory-A (agentic reader) achieves 64.7% overall MemoryAgentBench score, +19.2pp over the strongest baseline, leading all 4 capabilities: AR +12.5pp, TTL +4.4pp, LRU +25.4pp, SF +26.5pp. Vs hybrid variant Infini Memory-H (61.3%), agentic retrieval adds +3.4pp on average, largest gain on Selective Forgetting (+7.0pp). Single-hop vs multi-hop selective-forgetting gap: FC-SH 81.0% vs FC-MH 35.0% — write-time consolidation resolves single-document recency overrides but cannot enforce cross-document consistency spanning multiple topic documents updated at different times. Retrieval-strategy ablation on LongMemEval: single-shot summary selection only 41.7%, improved by adding BM25, further improved by the agentic reader (Fig.7/Table 2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Infini Memory's core design choice — plain-text, human-readable topic documents with explicit provenance metadata (seq/time/source) instead of an opaque vector/graph index (section 3.1-3.5, explicitly 'backend-light') — directly confirms MF's docs-as-truth typed-narrative Tier-1 stance.

The buffer-then-consolidate pipeline (CURRENT buffer -> periodic rewrite/split/merge into topic docs, section 3.3, Figure 3) is a concrete, deterministic mechanism for promoting transient write-time entries into durable maintained documents that MF's consolidation design could adopt directly.

The multi-hop selective-forgetting failure (FC-SH 81.0% vs FC-MH 35.0%, section 4.2 Discussion) is measured evidence that write-time consolidation alone cannot guarantee cross-document staleness/consistency, confirming MF's FIDELIDAD anchor needs an explicit mechanism beyond single-document rewriting.

The retrieval-strategy ablation (single-shot summary 41.7% -> +BM25 -> +agentic, Fig.7/Table 2) is a directly measured retrieval-layer comparison, confirming MF's stance that retrieval quality must be empirically measured rather than assumed from storage design alone.

notes: Ancla: Table 1 (full MemoryAgentBench results) + section 4.2 Discussion (FC-SH/FC-MH gap) + Fig.7/Table 2 (retrieval-strategy ablation). Clearly on-topic persistent-memory architecture paper.
